reden: Yes. Multiple findings in the audit content describe the same issue: eq() compares raw packed words (unwrap equality) and therefore treats numerically equal values encoded with different mantissa sizes (M vs L, i.e., with/without the L flag) as unequal. See entries such as “eq() compares raw words while toPackedFloat/divL produce multiple encodings of the same value,” “eq/le/ge give false for equal values stored as M and as L,” and similar. These match the vulnerability’s root cause (raw-word equality ignoring the L_MANTISSA_FLAG), affect the same function/path (Float128.eq), and would be fixed by the same mitigation (normalizing/decoding before compare).
